activity.notes: Abdallah ibn Yasin was the Maliki jurist and founding spiritual leader of the Almoravid movement. ATLAS uses 1054—the securely attested Sijilmasa conquest—as a representative start for the movement's territorial-political phase and 1059, the year of his death, as its end for this Activity. The start is approximate because his religious leadership began earlier than the first securely dated conquest.

sources.title: New Evidence on the Life of ‘Abdullāh B. Yāsīn and the Origins of the Almoravid Movement
sources.citation_text: Cambridge's Journal of African History study treats Abdallah ibn Yasin as the central early figure in the rise of the Almoravid movement and records the 1059 death tradition.

sources.title: Military Jihād against Muslims: ‘Abd Allāh b. Yāsīn and the Foundation of a Saharan Political Unit
sources.citation_text: The study describes Ibn Yasin as founder of the Almoravid movement, notes the 1054 Sijilmasa phase and his death in 1059, and characterizes the movement as an emerging political unit.
